newsitem.title: UK: Argentina's YPF plans 300 bln lira 5yr bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's YPF plans 300 bln lira 5yr bond.

text.p: Argentine oil and gas company YPF SA plans to launch a 300 billion lire bond with a five year maturity, a syndicate official at lead manager Chase Manhattan Bank said on Friday.
"I can confirm that Chase has got the mandate from YPF to launch the bond. It's a 300 billion lire deal, a five year fixed-rate, and roadshows begin on November 21," he said.
YPF surprised the markets last week when it pulled a proposed five-year $200 million Yankee bond, led by Merrill Lynch, postponing it until sometime in 1997.
Sources close to the lira deal said YPF decided to launch a lira bond despite pulling the Yankee bond because there is strong demand in the Italian currency sector.
The official gave no details of the spread or the coupon, but said approval from the Bank of Italy was still awaited.
Meanwhile, market sources said the Republic of Argentina was also expected to launch a 500 billion lire 10-year bond, but mooted lead manager Chase declined to comment.
